summary: Bearhead lookout site on Bearhead Peak, Sandoval County, NM; FFLA lists a gone crow's nest, a 1931 survey note describes a 38 ft tower, and the FS trail is unmaintained.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association, which classes it as a crow's nest

access.note: Forest Service hiking trail #9 to the summit; the trail page reports it has not been maintained since the 2011 Las Conchas Fire

visit.trail_note: Bearhead Peak Trail (Forest Trail 9), 0.5 miles from Bearhead Ridge Trail (Forest Trail 132); hiking only, medium difficulty, poor condition

events.note: Survey station description places a fire lookout tower about 38 ft high on the highest point of Bearhead Peak

evidence.supports: 1931 description of a fire lookout tower about 38 ft high, about 2.5 miles south of Bland
evidence.quote: ON HIGHEST POINT OF BEARHEAD PEAK, ABOUT 2.5 MI. S. OF BLAND, A FIRE LOOKOUT TOWER ABOUT 38 FT. HIGH.

evidence.supports: Station described by the U.S. Geological Survey in 1931
Sandoval County, Santa Fe National Forest
evidence.quote: New Mexico - Sandoval County - Santa Fe National Forest - 17N-4E-11

evidence.supports: Listed as a crow's nest and gone
Trail begins at the Bearhead Ridge Trail (Forest Trail 132) and ends on top of Bearhead Peak
evidence.quote: It begins at the Bearhead Ridge Trail (Forest Trail 132) and ends on top of Bearhead Peak.

evidence.supports: Trail is 0.5 miles long, Forest Trail 9
evidence.quote: The Bearhead Peak Trail (Forest Trail 9) is 0.5 miles long.

evidence.supports: Trail not maintained since the 2011 Las Conchas Fire
evidence.quote: The trail has not been maintained since the 2011 Las Conchas Fire.

evidence.supports: Trail limited to hiking, medium difficulty
evidence.quote: The trail is limited to hiking and rated as medium difficulty.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists a crow's nest (platform kind, which includes crow's nests); the 1931 survey description says a fire lookout tower about 38 ft high. Not resolved; the record keeps platform and the story reports both descriptions.

sources.title: Bearhead Peak Trail #9
sources.publisher: Santa Fe National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Story is about 150 words. The 1931 survey description is the only source that describes the structure, and it calls it a tower where FFLA says crow's nest; the record keeps platform, which covers crow's nests. No build date, builder, staffing or removal date was found in the fetched pages or two web searches. The Forest Service trail page gives no date for its maintenance note. Height 38 ft is converted to 11.6 m; the source says 'about'.
